analysis.one_liner: Sun Pharma is India's largest pharmaceutical company, making branded and generic medicines domestically while building a growing specialty drugs portfolio (such as Ilumya) in the US and other developed markets.
tags: US plant under FDA import alert
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sept 2026, reported 30 Oct 2026) showed revenue up 11.9% YoY to ₹16,199 crore, but reported PAT fell 36.2% YoY to ₹1,989 crore because of one-off charges of ₹1,268.8 crore - a US antitrust litigation settlement (₹922.7 crore) and costs tied to the pending Organon acquisition (₹346.2 crore). Separately, the Halol plant remains under a US FDA import alert after a June 2026 inspection flagged repeat quality issues, and Indian regulators halted eye-care product manufacturing at the Assam plant in August 2026 after a recall.
analysis.plain_terms: The 36% profit drop in the headlines looks alarming but is mostly a one-time accounting hit, not a collapse in the actual business - strip out the litigation settlement and deal costs, and adjusted profit was roughly flat to slightly up. The real tension is underneath: India sales are growing strongly (+17%), but US generics sales fell (-8%) and the specialty drug business that justifies the stock's premium price barely grew quarter-on-quarter. Add to that recurring US and Indian regulatory run-ins at manufacturing plants, and a large debt-funded acquisition (Organon) about to close.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27: revenue ₹16,199 crore (+11.9% YoY, +5.9% QoQ); EBITDA ₹4,744 crore, margin ~29.3%; reported PAT ₹1,989 crore (-36.2% YoY) distorted by ₹1,268.8 crore of one-off charges (litigation settlement + Organon deal costs) - adjusted PAT was ₹3,162 crore (+1.4% YoY), which is the more honest comparison. India formulations grew ~17% YoY (volume-led domestic strength); US formulations fell ~8% YoY. Global specialty revenue was $356 million, up 6.9% YoY but only $5 million higher than the prior quarter - management attributed this to a slowdown in US Ilumya sales, and guided that newer launches (Unloxcyt, Leqselvi) will matter more from FY28, with FY27 carrying elevated launch spend. Q1 FY27 (June quarter) had shown a cleaner picture: revenue +10.5% YoY, PAT +27% YoY.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 11.2% from its 30 July 2026 peak of ₹2,001, but there is no recent spin-off or demerger in the corporate-action data to adjust for here (last stock split was in 2013) - this is a genuine, fairly modest pullback, not a crash. Over longer periods the stock has clearly outperformed: +5.12% over 1 year versus Nifty's -8.13% and peer CIPLA's -7.44%; +58.83% over 3 years versus Nifty's 21.93%; and +137.01% over 5 years versus Nifty's 32.76% and CIPLA's 58.27%. Long-term shareholder returns have been strong and are not an artifact of corporate actions.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E is around 35x (approximate - exact current figure not independently verified), which is rich for a company with ROE near 15%. Why it looks expensive: the market is pricing in success of the specialty pipeline (Ilumya, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) and optionality from the pending Organon biosimilars deal, not just current-year earnings. Whether that premium is deserved is the open question - this quarter's specialty revenue barely grew sequentially, which is exactly the kind of data point that would need to reverse for the valuation to be justified rather than hopeful.
analysis.growth_read: Headline revenue growth of 11.9% YoY hides very different stories by segment: India formulations (+17% YoY) is genuine volume-and-price-led domestic franchise growth; US formulations (-8% YoY) is contraction, typical of US generic pricing pressure; and global specialty ($356m, +6.9% YoY but flat QoQ) is decelerating. So overall growth is currently carried by the domestic business, while the two growth engines the market is paying up for - US specialty and biosimilars (via Organon) - are either stalling or not yet contributing.
analysis.health_read: Core operations still convert to cash reasonably well - EBITDA margin held near 29% and adjusted PAT grew modestly - so this quarter's profit miss is a one-off accounting/cash-outflow event (litigation settlement, deal costs), not an operating breakdown. The more relevant risk here is business risk, not financial risk: repeated US FDA and Indian regulator issues at manufacturing plants (Halol import alert, Assam eye-care halt) are the kind of recurring operational problem that has dogged Sun Pharma for years. Financial risk is set to rise once the debt-financed Organon acquisition (~$11.75 billion enterprise value) closes, converting a historically net-cash balance sheet into a leveraged one - the post-deal debt figure could not be verified yet.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding appears to have dropped from 54.48% to 52.68% in the September 2026 quarter, but this was a shareholder-approved reclassification of certain promoter-group individuals into the 'public' category (effective 26 September 2026), not a sale - important not to read as promoters cashing out. Founder Dilip Shanghvi personally holds about 9.60% of the company with zero shares pledged, and total promoter pledging across the group is low, around 1.65%. Foreign institutional holding slipped to 14.4% from 16.1% a year earlier, while domestic institutions added, rising to 22.3% from 20.8% - domestic investors have been more constructive than foreign ones over the past year.
strengths: India formulations business grew ~17% YoY in Q2 FY27, the largest and most profitable part of the company
Adjusted PAT (ex one-offs) still grew 1.4% YoY and EBITDA margin held near 29.3% despite a one-off-heavy quarter
Stock has delivered 137% over 5 years versus Nifty's 32.76%, with promoter pledging at a low ~1.65% and founder Dilip Shanghvi holding 9.6% fully unpledged
Ilumya just received a new US approval for psoriatic arthritis (soft launch planned November 2026), a potential fresh growth lever
watchpoints: Halol plant remains under US FDA import alert after a June 2026 inspection found repeat quality issues dating back to a 2022 warning letter
Indian regulators (CDSCO) halted eye-care product manufacturing at the Assam plant in August 2026 following a recall covering roughly 332 batches across 11 brands
Global specialty revenue grew only $5 million quarter-on-quarter to $356 million, as US Ilumya sales slowed - the segment the premium valuation depends on is losing momentum

The $11.75 billion Organon acquisition, financed with cash and debt, is expected to close in early 2027 and will add leverage to a historically net-cash balance sheet; exact post-deal debt levels are not yet verified
analysis.one_thing: The next quarter's global specialty revenue growth (Ilumya, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) - a return to meaningful sequential growth would support the stock's premium valuation, while continued stalling, just as the debt-funded Organon deal closes, would undercut the core re-rating story.
analysis.data_notes: Q1/Q2 FY27 revenue, PAT and the one-off charge breakdown are corroborated across multiple independent sources and are consistent with the verified market data provided. Valuation ratios (P/E, ROE, ROCE, market cap, debt) came from aggregator sites without a confirmed as-of date and could not be fully cross-checked against a primary filing - treat as approximate; verify on Screener. The promoter shareholding drop is confirmed as a reclassification, not a sale. Next results date (expected late January 2027) is not officially confirmed, and product-level specialty revenue splits (Ilumya vs Winlevi vs Cequa) were not disclosed at that granularity in available sources.
